To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

baryonic feedback in the centers of galaxies reduces the central dark matter density of satellites by a factor of ~2-3, and that this reduction naturally explains the observed internal dynamics and low central densities of the Milky Way’s satellite galaxies.

1) the kinematics of the dwarf spheroidal satellites of the Milky Way and M 31 can be understood in the context of a Cold Dark Matter model if the effects of energetic supernova feedback and tidal stripping are included, and 2) this model naturally reproduces the observed low dark mass densities in these galaxies.
baryonic processes (feedback and tidal stripping) significantly reduce the mass of dark matter in the central regions (within 500 pc) of dwarf galaxies, which is why baryons matter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formation and evolution of dwarf galaxies in a cosmological context.
the internal dynamics of dwarf satellite galaxies.
the internal kinematics of the Milky Way dwarf satellite population and how they constrain the properties of dark matter in the Universe.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the kinematics of dwarf spheroidal satellites can be explained by baryonic physics and do not require alternative forms of dark mater.
baryons matter in the context of the internal kinematics of dwarf spheroidal galaxies.
the kinematics of dwarf satellites are consistent with the predictions of the standard CDM model, but only when baryonic physics is included.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the baryonic physics is the key for understanding the kinematics of the satellites.
we show the kinematics of dwarf satellites is a powerful probe of dark matter physics.
the baryonic content of galaxies is crucial to the formation and kinematics of their satellites.
The main takeaway from our work is that
baryonic effects in the central regions are the dominant effect that determines the kinematics and dynamics of dwarf spheroidal galaxies.
the kinematics of the Milky Way satellites are sensitive to the baryonic physics that drives the evolution of the satellites and the Milky Way halo.
